# Tutorial: your first index

Goal: go from a checkout to a queryable, freshness-tracked memory
of the repo — the artifact an agent loads before planning instead
of re-exploring from scratch.

## 1. Init

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda init
```

This writes a commented `kuda.toml` and a `.kuda/` skeleton. Open
the toml — the defaults are fully local and deterministic:

```toml
[extract]
kinds = ["manifest", "treesitter"]   # adapter names, tried in order

[summarize]
kind = "template"                    # deterministic cards

[store]
kind = "sqlite"
path = ".kuda/index.sqlite"
```

If `rust-analyzer` is on PATH you can add `"lsp"` to `kinds` —
extraction quality tiers up automatically (see
[extraction tiers](../explanation/architecture.md#extraction-tiers)).

## 2. Sync

```sh
kuda sync
```

Output:

```
sync /home/you/your-repo
indexed 19 module(s) at 3432d05
```

`sync` walks manifests, runs the tree-sitter symbol queries from
`data/langs/*`, summarizes each module into a card, and stores the
symbol/edge graph in sqlite. It writes:

| path                  | tier | commit?                  |
| --------------------- | ---- | ------------------------ |
| `.kuda/index.yaml`    | L0   | yes — the always-load card |
| `.kuda/modules/*.yaml`| L1   | yes — reviewable in diffs  |
| `.kuda/index.sqlite`  | L2   | no — rebuildable graph     |
| `.kuda/meta.json`     | meta | no — provenance record     |

## 3. Look at what it learned

```sh
kuda map
```

The L0 card: repo name, the module list, detected commands, and the
provenance block (`commit_sha`, file hashes, generator). This is the
\~1k-token blob an agent reads first.

```sh
kuda card kuda-store
```

An L1 card: purpose (from the manifest `description`), public API
symbols, dependency edges, `verify:` — the files to open before
trusting the card — and its own provenance.

## 4. Query

```sh
kuda find IndexStore
```

```
crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store
```

```sh
kuda dependents serde
```

```
kuda-cards --PackageDep--> serde
kuda-core --Imports--> serde
```

And the doc-sweep query — everything that mentions a name, useful
when a change must update code *and* docs and comments:

```sh
kuda refs SqliteStore --docs
```

## 5. Break it, then watch kuda notice

Edit any `crates/*/Cargo.toml` — change a `description` — and:

```sh
kuda status
```

```
drifted  kuda-store
19 fresh, 1 drifted (HEAD af26b8c)
```

`status` re-hashes each card's `verify:` files and compares with the
recorded provenance. `kuda sync` regenerates only what drifted.

## You have built

A committed, queryable, self-checking map of the repository. Point
agents at it — via `kuda mcp` or `kuda acp` — and they plan against
the map instead of grepping blindly.

Next: [serve it over MCP](../how-to/mcp.md) or
[index a multi-repo workspace](../how-to/multi-repo.md).

---

---
url: /kuda/how-to/multi-repo.md
---
# How-to: index a multi-repo workspace

For sibling checkouts — an org of repos that import each other —
kuda keeps one index per repo *and* answers cross-repo questions
over all of them.

## 1. Declare the workspace

Create `<checkout>/.kuda/workspace.yaml` (the directory
containing the sibling repos), or inside one repo's `.kuda/`:

```yaml
roots:
  - kuda
  - mimus
  - ../cli
  - ../lsp
```

Paths resolve relative to the file's directory. `[workspace]` in
`kuda.toml` documents the same intent:

```toml
[workspace]
roots = ["../cli", "../lsp"]
resolve_git_deps = true
```

## 2. Sync all roots

```sh
kuda sync --workspace
```

```
sync /home/you/GitHub/9aia/kuda
indexed 19 module(s) at af26b8c
sync /home/you/GitHub/9aia/mimus
indexed 15 module(s) at 323421e
```

Each root gets its own `.kuda/` artifacts — the per-repo indexes
stay independent and committable in their own repos.

## 3. Query across the set

```sh
kuda dependents kuda-core --workspace
```

Edges found in *every* root's store are merged — so an import of
`kuda-core` inside `mimus` shows up alongside internal users.
That is the impact-analysis query that matters for a breaking
change: "who calls this, anywhere in the org".

## 4. Git dependency edges

`resolve_git_deps = true` records the intent for the extractor
tier that maps `git = "…"` manifest dependencies onto sibling
checkouts — turning "depends on github.com/x/y" into "depends on
the sibling repo y". Until that lands, cross-repo edges come from
module-name matching across the merged stores.

## Current limits

* `find` and `refs` remain per-root; `dependents` is the merged
  query today.
* Cards are generated per root — there is no aggregate workspace
  card yet. Compose one from `kuda map` output across roots.

url: /kuda/how-to/mcp.md

# How-to: serve the index over MCP

`kuda mcp` exposes the index as tools to MCP-capable agents
(Devin, Cursor, Claude Code, Zed, …). It is a stdio JSON-RPC
server — no ports, no daemon.

## Run

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda mcp
```

## Tools

| tool          | query                                   |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `repo_card`   | L0 blob — the always-load summary       |
| `module_card` | L1 card + freshness for one module      |
| `find`        | symbol -> file:line                     |
| `dependents`  | reverse dep edges (impact analysis)     |
| `refs`        | code + docs/comments mentions           |
| `status`      | provenance drift vs HEAD                |

## Register with your agent

stdio servers are declared in the client's MCP config — the shape
varies, but it is always "command + args":

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kuda": { "command": "kuda", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Run it from a repo that has been `kuda sync`'d — the tools read
`.kuda/` at call time, so a re-`sync` is picked up without
restarting the server.

## Verify the handshake

```sh
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"find","arguments":{"name":"IndexStore"}}}' \
  | kuda mcp
```

Two replies: the `initialize` result, then a `content[0].text`
body like `crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store`.

## Trust model

Cards are hypotheses. Every `module_card` response includes the
`verify:` file list — agents should open those files before
acting on card content, and `status` tells them whether the whole
index has drifted. See [architecture](../explanation/architecture.md#trust-model).

See also: [ACP surface](acp.md) — same index, the other wire
protocol.

---

---
url: /kuda/how-to/acp.md
---
# How-to: the ACP surface

`kuda acp` speaks the Agent Client Protocol — the editor↔agent
wire protocol used by Zed and supported by agent clients such as
cline and Cursor. Where `kuda mcp` exposes *tools*, `kuda acp`
exposes the index as an *agent* you can prompt.

## Run

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda acp     # stdio JSON-RPC server
```

## Prompts

The session/prompt method accepts compact query strings:

| prompt              | returns                                  |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `find <symbol>`     | `file:line kind module` hits             |
| `dependents <name>` | reverse dep edges                        |
| `card <module>`     | the module card YAML                     |
| `map` / `status`    | the L0 card (fallback for anything else) |

Replies stream back as session/update notifications with
`agent_message_chunk` content, then a `stopReason: end_turn`
result.

## Verify

```sh
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"'"$PWD"'","mcpServers":[]}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"session/prompt","params":{"sessionId":"kuda-default","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"find IndexStore"}]}}' \
  | kuda acp
```

You get `agentInfo`, a `sessionId`, an `agent_message_chunk`
carrying `crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs:9 Trait kuda-store`, and
`end_turn`.

## Which protocol when?

* **MCP** — the agent already has tool-use wired and you want the
  index as callable tools. Most current clients.
* **ACP** — you want kuda to appear as an *agent* inside an
  ACP-speaking client, sharing its own session model.

Both read the same `.kuda/` artifacts — pick per client, or run
both.

# How-to: add a language

Per-language knowledge is data, not code. A new language means a
new `data/langs/*.toml` descriptor — the extractors' vocabulary
stays fixed.

## The descriptor

`data/langs/rust.toml` is the template:

```toml
name = "rust"
extensions = [".rs"]
manifests = ["Cargo.toml"]          # module-boundary markers
grammar = "rust"                    # adapter id — see below

# Tree-sitter symbol query. Captures are @name.<kind> where
# <kind> maps to SymbolKind: function|type|trait|const|module|macro.
symbol_query = '''
(function_item name: (identifier) @name.function)
(struct_item name: (type_identifier) @name.type)
...
'''
```

| field          | used by                                  |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | reports, LSP `languageId`                |
| `extensions`   | both extractors' file walking            |
| `manifests`    | package graph + module attribution       |
| `grammar`      | `kuda-treesitter` language registry      |
| `symbol_query` | optional; falls back to a builtin        |

## What the adapter id controls

`grammar` is looked up in the adapter's registry — the match arm
inside `kuda-treesitter::language()`. Today that registry has one
entry (`rust`). Adding e.g. `python` needs the compiled
`tree-sitter-python` crate as a dependency plus one arm — an
adapter change, not an engine change. Descriptors for languages
without a compiled grammar still get `manifest` extraction
(module graph) for free.

## Writing a symbol query

1. Find the grammar's `node-types.json` (in the grammar repo) for
   the node names your language uses.
2. Capture the *name* child of each public-ish item as
   `@name.<kind>` — the kind suffix must match `SymbolKind`
   names or it lands in `Other`.
3. Test locally: put the query in `symbol_query`, run
   `kuda sync`, then `kuda find <a-symbol>`.

## Deploying descriptors

The CLI embeds `data/langs/*.toml` at build time. Adding a file
there + rebuilding is the whole distribution path today — a
config point for user-supplied descriptor dirs is a TODO item.

# How-to: summarizers

`kuda-cards` turns extractions into the committed YAML artifacts.
Two shipping adapters: `template` (deterministic) and `acp`
(agent-written prose); `llm` is parked — ACP is the semantic path.

## `acp` — agent-written cards

```toml
[summarize]
kind = "acp"
acp_cmd = "env CLINE_PROVIDER=cline-pass CLINE_MODEL=cline-free/mimo-v2.6-flash cline --acp"
# NOTE: provider/model are env vars, not CLI flags — -P/-m are
# ignored in ACP mode.
```

`sync` spawns the agent once per run (one session, reused across
modules) and sends each module a session/prompt asking for
`purpose:`/`invariants:`/`notes:` grounded in the file list. The
agent's prose fills the card's `purpose` + `notes` regions —
`api`/`deps`/`verify`/`provenance` stay mechanical.

Protocol notes:

* session/request_permission from the agent is auto-answered
  with the first option — required, or the prompt deadlocks
* Any ACP-capable agent works: `cline --acp`, `zed agent`,
  `gemini --experimental-acp`, …
* Auth lives in the agent — kuda holds no keys
* Agent failure → silent `template` fallback per module

## `template` (default, shipping)

Deterministic, zero-model. Each module card's `purpose` comes
from the manifest `description` field (Cargo.toml
`[package].description`, package.json `description`); `api` lists
the extracted public symbols; `deps` lists the module's edges;
`verify:` lists the files the card was built from.

Because it is mechanical, `template` output is stable — the same
inputs always produce the same card, so diffs mean real change.
That is the property you want in committed, reviewed artifacts.

## `llm` (parked)

A direct-provider adapter (`provider`/`model` + keyring) is in
the backlog — ACP is preferred because it is agent-agnostic and
key-free. Same grounding rules apply when it lands: cite files or
stay silent, never clobber `verify:` or human `notes:`.

## Incremental sync

`sync` compares each module's input-file hashes with the committed
card's `provenance.hashes` before calling the summarizer — identical
means the card is reused and the agent is never prompted. Change one
file and only that module re-summarizes; the agent spend is
per-drift, not per-sync.

## File-tier cards

`file_cards = true` under `[summarize]` adds an L1.5 level: every
source file gets a `.kuda/files/<module>/<file>.yaml` card. Files
are split into ~1.5k-char semantic chunks (tree-sitter aware via
text-splitter), budgeted to ~14k chars per prompt, and each card
carries its own blob hash — an unchanged file never re-prompts.

# Command-Line Help for `kuda`

This document contains the help content for the `kuda` command-line program.

**Command Overview:**

* [`kuda`↴](#kuda)
* [`kuda init`↴](#kuda-init)
* [`kuda sync`↴](#kuda-sync)
* [`kuda status`↴](#kuda-status)
* [`kuda map`↴](#kuda-map)
* [`kuda card`↴](#kuda-card)
* [`kuda find`↴](#kuda-find)
* [`kuda dependents`↴](#kuda-dependents)
* [`kuda refs`↴](#kuda-refs)
* [`kuda mcp`↴](#kuda-mcp)
* [`kuda acp`↴](#kuda-acp)
* [`kuda doctor`↴](#kuda-doctor)

## `kuda`

A hippocampus for your codebase — repo memory: index, query, verify

**Usage:** `kuda [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/ scaffold
* `sync` — Incremental index (hash -> extract -> summarize -> store)
* `status` — Provenance vs HEAD: per-card drift report
* `map` — Render the L0 repo card (the always-load blob)
* `card` — Module card + freshness
* `find` — Symbol -> file:line
* `dependents` — Reverse dep lookup — impact analysis
* `refs` — Code + docs/comments mentions — the doc-sweep query
* `mcp` — Serve the index over MCP (stdio)
* `acp` — Speak ACP — Agent Client Protocol surface for any agent client (zed, cline, cursor)
* `doctor` — Extractor/store/config health

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (else $KUDA_CONFIG, ./kuda.toml, ~/.config/kuda/kuda.toml)
* `--workspace` — Workspace mode — all roots in .kuda/workspace.yaml

## `kuda init`

Detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/ scaffold

**Usage:** `kuda init`

## `kuda sync`

Incremental index (hash -> extract -> summarize -> store)

**Usage:** `kuda sync [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--full` — Rebuild everything, ignoring content-hash freshness

## `kuda status`

Provenance vs HEAD: per-card drift report

**Usage:** `kuda status`

## `kuda map`

Render the L0 repo card (the always-load blob)

**Usage:** `kuda map`

## `kuda card`

Module card + freshness

**Usage:** `kuda card <MODULE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<MODULE>`

## `kuda find`

Symbol -> file:line

**Usage:** `kuda find <SYMBOL>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<SYMBOL>`

## `kuda dependents`

Reverse dep lookup — impact analysis

**Usage:** `kuda dependents <NAME>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`

## `kuda refs`

Code + docs/comments mentions — the doc-sweep query

**Usage:** `kuda refs [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`

###### **Options:**

* `--docs` — Only docs/comments/markdown mentions

## `kuda mcp`

Serve the index over MCP (stdio)

**Usage:** `kuda mcp`

## `kuda acp`

Speak ACP — Agent Client Protocol surface for any agent client (zed, cline, cursor)

**Usage:** `kuda acp`

## `kuda doctor`

Extractor/store/config health

**Usage:** `kuda doctor`

# Config — `kuda.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `RepoCfg` | optional | — |
| `extract` | `ExtractCfg` | optional | — |
| `summarize` | `SummarizeCfg` | optional | — |
| `store` | `StoreCfg` | optional | — |
| `cards` | `CardsCfg` | optional | — |
| `workspace` | `WorkspaceCfg` | optional | — |

## `[repo]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | optional | Defaults to the directory basename. |
| `root` | `path` | optional | Repo root; default = the toml's dir. |

## `[extract]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | `list` | optional | Impl kinds tried in order: "manifest" | "treesitter" | "lsp". |
| `lsp_server` | `string` | optional | Server command for the lsp adapter (per-language later). |
| `exclude` | `list` | optional | Extra dir/file names skipped during walks, on top of the built-in set (`.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, `.kuda`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `.cache`, `.next`, `vendor`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `coverage`, `generated`, …). Keeps generated/vendored content out of the index, provenance hashes, and agent prompts — direct agent-cost control. |

## `[summarize]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | "template" (deterministic, default) | "acp" (agent-spawned). |
| `acp_cmd` | `string` | optional | ACP agent spawn command for kind="acp" — e.g. `env CLINE_PROVIDER=… CLINE_MODEL=… cline --acp`. |
| `file_cards` | `bool` | optional | L1.5 per-file chunked summaries (`.kuda/files/`). ~10-50x module-card prompt count; per-file hash gate bounds steady state. |
| `provider` | `string` | optional | Provider id for the llm adapter (parked); key resolves via secrets chain. |
| `model` | `string` | optional | — |

## `[store]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | — |
| `path` | `path` | optional | L2 index path — rebuildable, gitignored. |

## `[cards]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | optional | Committed artifacts dir: index.yaml + modules/\*.yaml. |

## `[workspace]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `roots` | `Vec<PathBuf>` | optional | Sibling repo roots indexed together. |
| `resolve_git_deps` | `bool` | optional | Resolve `git = ".../org/repo"` manifest deps to siblings. |

## Constraints

* `queue = "all"` rejects `cancel_running = true` at load —
  killing a run would silently drop a promised commit.
* `runner.kind` and `trigger.kind`/`status.kind` resolve to impl
  crates; unknown kinds fail at `kuda doctor`/startup.
* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.

# Reference: card schema

Two artifact files, both committed YAML under `.kuda/` (location
configurable via `[cards].dir`).

## `.kuda/index.yaml` — the L0 repo card

```yaml
name: kuda                     # repo display name
root: /abs/path/to/repo
purpose: ''                    # manifest/tagline — human-editable
modules:                       # sorted module names
- kuda-core
- kuda-store
commands:                      # detected verify/build commands
- cargo check
- cargo test --workspace
provenance:
  files: [crates/kuda-store/Cargo.toml, ...]
  hashes: [sha1, ...]          # git hash-object per file
  commit_sha: af26b8c…
  generated_at: '1712345678'   # unix seconds
  generator: kuda/0.1.0
```

## `.kuda/modules/<name>.yaml` — an L1 module card

```yaml
name: kuda-store
path: crates/kuda-store/Cargo.toml
purpose: Store port — IndexStore trait          # manifest description
api:                           # extracted public symbols
- IndexStore
- SqliteStore
deps:                          # outgoing edges
- from: kuda-store
  to: kuda-core
  kind: PackageDep
notes: ''                      # HUMAN-OWNED — preserved on regen
verify:                        # files to open before trusting
- crates/kuda-store/src/lib.rs
provenance:
  files: [...]
  hashes: [...]
  commit_sha: …
  generated_at: '…'
  generator: kuda-template/0.1.0
```

## Provenance semantics

`files` + `hashes` are git `hash-object` digests of the card's
inputs at sync time. `kuda status` (and `mimus audit`) re-hash
the same files and compare — a mismatch marks the card `drifted`.
`commit_sha` records the index point in history; `generator`
records which adapter produced the card so format drift is
auditable.

## Ownership

Machine fields (`api`, `deps`, `provenance`) are regenerated on
every `sync`. `notes:` and `purpose:` (when hand-edited past the
manifest default) are the human regions — a real merge story is
a TODO; today regen overwrites `purpose` only when it still
equals the old machine value.

# Explanation: architecture

kuda answers one question — *"what does this project look like,
right now, in a form an agent can load?"* — and treats a wrong
answer as worse than none.

## The pipeline

```
repos ──► extract ──► summarize ──► index ──► store ──► serve
          │             │            │         │         │
   adapters:        adapters:    graph +   sqlite    cli |
   manifest         template     cards    + yaml    mcp | acp
   treesitter       (llm planned)  provenance
   lsp
```

**Extract** is mechanical — no model, fully rerunnable. It pulls
symbols, package structure, and import edges.

**Summarize** turns each module's extraction into an L1 card —
committed YAML humans review in diffs.

**Index** merges everything into the symbol/dependency graph with
per-node provenance.

**Serve** is read-side only: `find`, `dependents`, `refs`,
`card`, `map`, `status` — plus the MCP and ACP wire surfaces.

## The tiers of memory

* **L0 repo card** (`.kuda/index.yaml`) — the ~1k-token
  always-load blob: purpose, module map, commands, provenance.
* **L1 module cards** (`.kuda/modules/*.yaml`) — fetched on
  demand when planning touches a module.
* **L1.5 file cards** (`.kuda/files/<module>/*.yaml`) — per-source-file
  `purpose` written by the semantic tier (opt-in,
  `[summarize] file_cards = true`). Files are chunked with a
  code-aware splitter (tree-sitter boundaries via text-splitter),
  fed to the agent, and hash-gated per file.
* **L2 graph** (`.kuda/index.sqlite`) — symbols, edges both
  directions, per-file hashes; gitignored, rebuildable, the query
  substrate.
* **L3** — the source itself. Memory is an index *into* code,
  never a replacement.

Committed L0/L1/L1.5 + ignored L2 is deliberate: cards are reviewed
prose, the graph is derived state.

## Incremental sync

`sync` is diff-driven end to end:

1. One walk groups manifests + source files by module (manifest
   package names, not dir names — `kuda-docs`, not `docs`).
2. Every file gets an in-process git blob hash — no subprocess
   per file.
3. Hashes are compared against the store's `files` table —
   unchanged modules are never re-parsed; a changed file re-parses
   only its own module.
4. Cards whose provenance matches are reused verbatim — the
   summarizer (and the agent, in `acp` mode) is only invoked for
   drift.

Steady-state on a warm index is sub-second; agent spend is
per-drift, never per-sync. Deleted files and vanished modules are
detected by the same diff — their cards and store rows are
removed.

## Extraction tiers

Best-available wins, configured per repo via `[extract].kinds`:

* `manifest` — free, no parser: package graph + module
  boundaries from Cargo.toml/package.json/pyproject/go.mod.
* `treesitter` — grammar+query data from `data/langs/*`:
  symbols and `use`/import edges in ~any language.
* `lsp` — `documentSymbol` against a real server
  (`lsp_server = "rust-analyzer"`); the strongest signal where a
  server exists. Absent server = silent skip.

See [adding a language](../how-to/languages.md) — knowledge lives
in descriptor files; adding one is a data change.

## Language as data

Per-language knowledge — grammar refs, symbol queries, manifest
names — lives in `data/langs/*`, not in extractor code. The
adapters' vocabulary (`language()` registries, `SymbolKind`,
`EdgeKind`) is the only fixed part.

## Ports and adapters

`kuda-core` holds domain types only (`Symbol`, `ModuleCard`,
`Provenance`, `Claim`-free config). Every concern is a trait
crate + adapter crates:

* `kuda-extract` → `kuda-manifest`, `kuda-treesitter`, `kuda-lsp`
* `kuda-store` → `kuda-store-sqlite`
* `kuda-summarize` → `kuda-template`, (`kuda-llm` planned)
* `kuda-vcs` → `kuda-git`; `kuda-config` → `kuda-config-toml`;
  `kuda-secret` → `kuda-keyring`, `kuda-dotenv`

New capability = new adapter crate, not a core rewrite.

## Trust model

Every artifact carries `provenance {files, hashes, commit_sha,
generator}` — `kuda status` re-hashes and reports drift per card.
Cards end with `verify:` — the files an agent should open before
acting on the card. Memory is a hypothesis that narrows the
search space; the code remains the only truth. `mimus audit`
independently re-verifies card provenance — memory with an
external falsifier.

---
url: /kuda/explanation/release-model.md
---
# The release model

kuda releases itself — there is no hosted CI and no release tool
in the loop. Two deliberate phases:

## Phase 1 — the explicit seed

`kuda deploy release` runs once, by hand: it reads cargo metadata,
topologically orders the workspace's path-dependency graph,
`cargo publish`es every member, tags `{repo}-v{version}`, and pushes
the tag.

Why explicit? Publishing is the **only irreversible step** in the
whole system. Queues, runs, and statuses are all idempotent and
local; a crate version on crates.io is forever. Everything else in
kuda fires on push — the seed doesn't. (`--dry-run` prints the
order and tag without touching anything.)

## Phase 2 — push-driven forever after

From then on a release is *just another kuda job*: a push to `main`
hits the webhook, queues latest-wins, and runs `scripts/release.sh`
in a detached worktree under the shell runner.

The script:

1. diffs crate paths since the last `kuda-v*` tag
2. `cargo set-version --bump patch` on touched crates only (the cli
   republishes on any change — it's the install artifact)
3. `cargo publish`es them in dep order
4. tags `kuda-vX.Y.Z`, builds host-arch binaries with `cargo dist`,
   uploads to a GitHub Release via `gh`

The 5-minute sleep at the top isn't a hack — it's the debounce
window. Combined with `queue = "latest"` + `cancel_running`, rapid
push bursts collapse to one release of the newest sha; killed runs
get an honest "cancelled" status.

## Why this shape

* **No release-plz / GHA**: the point of the project is that CI is a
  local loop — depending on hosted CI to ship it would be
  self-defeating. `scripts/release.sh` is deliberately boring bash so it can
  run as a plain `cmd` under `runner.kind = "shell"`.
* **Latest-wins, not `all`**: a release that misses an intermediate
  push loses nothing — the tag lands on HEAD, which contains
  everything. `queue = "all"` is for pipelines where each sha's run
  is individually meaningful.
* **Explicit over automatic**: a wrong tag or half-published
  workspace is far worse than a delayed release; the boundary sits
  exactly at irreversibility.

Host prerequisites: `cargo-edit`, `cargo-dist`, `gh`, and
`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (env → keyring → env file). Multi-arch
binaries arrive when the remote-runner pair lands — see TODO.

---
# kuda vs the alternatives

## vs grep + re-read every session

|                       | grep/ripgrep          | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| find a symbol         | fast, per-query       | fast — plus kind + card    |
| "what depends on X"   | manual, cross-repo pain | one query                |
| overall comprehension | none                  | L0 card in ~1k tokens      |
| freshness             | always current        | provenance-checked         |
| doc/comment mentions  | same grep             | unified `refs --docs`      |

## vs embeddings / RAG

|                       | RAG store             | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| fuzzy semantic lookup | strong                | (optional store adapter later)|
| dep graph, provenance | weak                  | first-class                |
| staleness             | opaque                | explicit sha/hash diff     |
| determinism           | model-dependent       | `template` = deterministic |

## vs LSP alone

|                       | LSP                   | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| cross-file refs       | strong (per language) | `lsp` adapter reuses them     |
| needs a running server| yes                   | only for the `lsp` tier    |
| prose/cards           | none                  | L1/L0 artifacts            |
| persistence           | session-scoped        | committed + rebuildable    |

Trade-off: kuda adds an index step and committed artifacts — the
payoff is that "overall comprehension" becomes a fixed ~1k-token
load instead of a per-session expedition.

# Getting started

Pick by what you need to do.

* **Tutorials** (learn): [first-run](tutorials/first-run.md)
* **How-to** (tasks): [multi-repo](how-to/multi-repo.md) ·
  [mcp](how-to/mcp.md) ·
  [llm summarizer](how-to/llm-summarizer.md)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli](reference/cli.md) ·
  [config](reference/config.md) ·
  [crate api](reference/crate-api.md)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](explanation/architecture.md) ·
  [release model](explanation/release-model.md) ·
  [comparison](comparison.md) — vs grep / RAG

Install:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/kuda kuda
```

First index:

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda init    # detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/
kuda sync    # incremental index -> .kuda/ artifacts
kuda status  # provenance vs HEAD
kuda map     # the L0 card — what agents load first
```
